subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Opium Wars: Tea's Deadly Trade
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Opium Wars: Tea's Deadly Trade.

hook.text: Britain's tea addiction created a huge trade deficit with China. The solution? Flood China with opium to balance the books.

buildup.text: By the 1830s, Britain imported millions of pounds of Chinese tea but had little that China wanted to buy in return.

discovery.text: Britain grew opium in India and smuggled it into China—creating millions of addicts and reversing the trade deficit.

twist.text: When China tried to stop the opium trade, Britain declared war. Two Opium Wars forced China to accept the drug trade.

climax.text: Tea's demand fueled one of history's most devastating drug crises. The cup of tea in London had a dark trail back to China.

punchline.text: A cup of tea, a trail of opium, two wars. Demand has consequences.

quiz.question: Why did Britain sell opium to China?
options: To balance a trade deficit caused by massive tea imports from China

details.summary: Britain's insatiable demand for Chinese tea in the 19th century created a massive trade deficit. To balance it, Britain illegally exported opium from India to China. When China resisted, two Opium Wars erupted, reshaping Asian geopolitics and devastating Chinese society for generations.
details.whyItMatters: The Opium Wars show how a simple beverage preference escalated into one of modern history's most consequential and destructive international conflicts.
takeaways: Britain's tea addiction created a huge trade deficit with China
Opium exports were used to balance the economic gap
Two wars resulted, with lasting consequences for China and Asia

faq.question: How did British tea consumption lead to the Opium Wars with China?
faq.answer: Britain imported enormous quantities of tea from China but had little China wanted in return, draining silver reserves. Selling Indian opium to China created demand that balanced trade, but China's attempts to stop the opium flow sparked the wars.

faq.question: What were the major consequences of the Opium Wars for China?
faq.answer: China was forced to cede Hong Kong to Britain, open numerous ports to foreign trade, and accept unequal treaties. The wars also triggered widespread opium addiction and are considered the start of China's century of humiliation.
